questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: English speaking country, non-european, college-town

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was challenging and it takes a lot of time. The advisors are really nice and helps a lot, but you need to commit a lot of hours to sorting out everything. I recommend finding someone whos been to the place before. It was stressfull but it is all so worth it

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: UCSB are amazing at helping you, they will answer every email really fast and you can contact them anytime.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I found housing in a Facebook group, I recommend living off campus, because people on campus are typically really young and also living in Isla Vista is a really unique experience

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer:
- You should live (sublease) in Isla Vista (right on the beach!!, big houses with a lot of people, very social, older people compared to on-campus) - Iris only 5 min bike /15 min walk to campus  (basically on-campus almost)
- It is very expensive and you will have to share a room with a least one person
- it is a big college town and a lot of partying (however everything needs to be quite after 00) 
- Good idea to FaceTime the people before you sign anything - also try not to pay anything before you see the place 


Be aware that you dont sublease from a "satellite house" if you are not willing to have parties at your house every weekend - this is where older fraternities members live and they do house parties all the time, which messes up the houses a lot (sometimes they dont tell you this if you dont ask!)

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I loved my housing, but it was a little stressfull to find, I was very lucky and got contacted after I made a post in a Facebook group. There is a housing crisis in UCSB and therefore rent is really expensive I paid 1400$ /month for a double in a house with 13 girls. My house was in good condition, but some of the houses in IV are really bad, make sure to search up the house and look at pictures

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: There is a lot of different processes and the KU advisors are really good at explaining it - and the UCSb platform is really easy to navigate

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: KU advisors meetings, powerpoints

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I went for my first semester of my masters, so I was very free in choosing courses, I did get almost everything I want , but the registration process in the US is very different from home and the spots fill up quickly

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Ask the advisors about everything that confuses you, they are really good at helping. Look at all the courses on GOLD and write them down before your pass time - make sure to get your prerequisites in time

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The courses in my major, Political Science, is defiantly easier in the US than at home, but I choose a lot of small classes with about twenty people, so there was a lot of discussion, which made a bit more fun and challenging, as English is my second language.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Very different, a lot of sections with mandatory participation, home work throughout the week, essays throughout the week, a midterm final - everything you do I the class during the quarter counts for your final grade

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Comperative Media and Politics 
Islam and Government
Contemporary Political Theory
Modern Political Theory 
Feminist Theories 
Indigenous Movements

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Do something outside your major, universities in the US let you do that and they offer a lot of niche and interesting courses. Do smaller course, o it is easier to meet people.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I did a lot of trips, which ended up being very expensive, also groceries is super expensive in California

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Insurance, Vaccines, Food, Utilities, hygiene products, Ubers, renting cars

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Everything is available, there is a club for everything and a gym, pool, basketball/soccer/tennis/padel courts that you can use for free as a student

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Excursion club to go on camping trips and hikes !!!

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Visit the national parks, The US has so much insane nature. Yosemite was my favourite place ! Also just recommend during trips to the nearby cities in California, but also try to travel to other states because it is a very different experience

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It is a very different culture, but there is so many exchange students which makes is easier because you are all in it together.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Be open, say yes to everything as the Americans are very open and friendly and will invite you to whatever event they are having.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The quarter system could be a little challenging sometime as everything yo do in the course counts and you often have participation. Needing a car to go must places was also very challenging and getting groceries could be annoying - however you can bike or take the bus

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The openness, the college town experience, the outdoor / activity scene, a lot of hikes and surfing!! I liked to go to office hours to speak to the professors as they are very interested in the students and love to speak about the exchange experience

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Make sure to make a budget, it will be very expensive and there is a lot of administrative work. BUT it is very worth it and it will 100% be the best experience

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Meeting so many interesting people, living on the beach in California, trying a lot of new things

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Getting my Visa as the process got shut down by Trump in the middle of it

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
